articleTitle: A New Soil Moisture Sensor Based on Matryoshka DGS
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: With the continuous evolution of telecommunications systems, the use of wireless sensor networks also grows, which demands the development of sensors that can be integrated into remote units. In this context, this paper introduces a soil moisture sensor based on matryoshka DGS. The matryoshka DGS is described, including first approach design equations. The proposed sensor is L1-shaped, which allows its insertion into the soil, as usual in other sensor types. The gravimetric soil moisture, and how it was carried out in this paper, is outlined. A prototype was fabricated and applied to two soil types (sandy and garden soils), achieving a good resolution between the dry and saturated states. Despite the attractive and encouraging results, one of the most important paper contributions is the introduced sensor concept, which can be optimized for different applications, taking advantage of matryoshka DGS characteristics. Furthermore, considering the integration of the sensor in a remote unit, it is still possible to take advantage of an already available RF stage.

articleTitle: Performance of Tb Glass Used to Fabricate Special Optical Fiber as a Discrete Current Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: The performance of Tb glass used to fabricate special optical fiber is evaluated as a discrete magnetic sensor and compared with rare-earth iron garnet (RIG) based discrete sensor and silica based optical fiber sensors. The proposed material has a Verdet constant 28.8 times higher than silica. Employing a sample of Tb-glass of 5 mm length a measured sensitivity 15.6 times lower than the RIG-based sensor was achieved, proving that the proposed material can be used both as a discrete bulk element as well as an optical fiber sensing element presenting a trade-off between the silica fibers and RIG elements which cannot be pulled to form an optical fiber.

articleTitle: An Exploratory Analysis for Carrying Out a Digital Transformation of Radio Broadcasting in Colombia and Latin America
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: Radio broadcasting is a public service with a great impact on the social development of Colombia. Its objective is to guarantee the right to information, recreation, free expression, and personality development. In Colombia, the radio broadcasting service covers almost all the country, this somehow reduces the existing gap in populations that are not digitally connected. This paper proposes an exploration of the current state of radio broadcasting in Colombia and digital radio broadcasting in the world, to review the possible implementation of this technology, so its focus is informative. In addition, it is intended to analytically compare the penetration of new digital radio broadcasting technologies in the world with respect to the penetration in Latin American countries.

articleTitle: Security Enhanced Encryption on Color Modulation of Visible Light Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: Visible Light Communication (VLC) is an emerging technology that harnesses the visible light spectrum within the field of optical wireless communication (OWC). It aims to deliver high-speed data transfer rates, enhanced security, and improved energy efficiency in access networks. However, the physical layer of VLC systems is vulnerable to eavesdroppers, making it crucial to implement secure transmission techniques. This study explores a VLC system that enhances privacy levels in wireless optical communication systems through two techniques: a color modulation scheme and a hyperchaotic three-dimensional map. Through successful error-free testing at a wireless link distance of 1 meter and a symbol transmission rate of 2 Baud, this solution has demonstrated its potential for secure information communication for smartphone users.

articleTitle: Comparison of Two Sensors with Matryoshka Defected Ground Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This paper presents two different types of sensors that are based on the matryoshka geometry with a Defected Ground Structure (DGS). The main idea is to compare the sensor's response for close and open matryoshka rings. The proposed DGS sensor geometry is outlined, and initial design equations are presented. Two prototypes were fabricated and characterized. Very good agreement is obtained between numerical simulation and experimental results for the open configuration. Moreover, the resonance frequency determined using the proposed design equations presents a good agreement too. To verify the matryoshka DGS sensors' response, a mixture of distilled water and isopropyl alcohol was characterized, and the corresponding calibration curves are compared. Finally, the matryoshka DGS sensors, are compared also in terms of miniaturization and sensitivity.

articleTitle: Miniaturization of DGS Filter Based on Matryoshka Geometry Using Calcium Cobaltite Ceramic
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This paper introduces the use of calcium cobaltite ceramic of composition Ca3Co4O9, C349, for miniaturization of a defected-ground-structure (DGS) filter based on matryoshka geometry. Initially applied to frequency selective surfaces, matryoshka geometry has been successfully applied to filters and sensors. Recently, this geometry has been used in a DGS filter achieving a decrease in the resonant frequency of up to 47.2%, when compared to traditional geometries such as dumbbells. Despite this result being quite interesting, the use of a small calcium cobaltite ceramic disk, practically without increasing the original area occupied by the DGS, further reduces the resonant frequency, achieving approximately 43.0% of the DGS-matryoshka geometry without the ceramic disk, which corresponds to an occupied area of approximately <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.062\lambda_{0} {\times}0.062\lambda_{0}$</tex>. Furthermore, for the same DGS-matryoshka geometry, different positions of the ceramic disk can be used to obtain different resonant frequencies. Numerical and experimental results are presented, verifying a good agreement.

articleTitle: Mechanical Wave Detection Through Polyurethane Foam Using Optical Fiber Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: In recent years, distributed acoustic sensing has garnered significant interest in seismic monitoring due to its sensitivity to low frequencies, continuity of measurement in both time and space and the capacity to provide vast amounts of data regarding the conditions of large structures. This study aims to develop a metrological characterization system to evaluate the performance of the distributed acoustic sensing systems to reconstruct the mechanical wavefront and measure its propagation speed in polyurethane foams. The wave propagation speed measured using distributed acoustic sensing is compared with optical fiber Bragg grating sensors and piezoelectric accelerometer, and the difference is less than 1.5%. The results demonstrate that it is possible to reconstruct the mechanical wavefront using both instrumented sensors, thus validating the application of a distributed acoustic sensing system for mechanical wave measurement in polyurethane foams.

articleTitle: High Speed Terahertz TDS Scanner for Automatic Detection of Defects
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: Automatic detection of defects in glass fibre reinforced polymer (GFRP) based on a terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (TDS) system is presented. We measured a GFRP sample with 15 round delaminations of different sizes by means of a TDS reflective scanner. The algorithm acquired a series of C-scans, which were then analysed using two complementary methods - adaptive threshold and Gaussian valley emphasis. 100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> of defects were successfully detected.

articleTitle: Effects of Gaussian Apodization on the Propagation of Two-Dimensional Discrete Frozen Waves in Homogeneous Media
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: In this work, we present an approach to design longitudinally-structured light sheets when apodized by Gaussian profiles and analyze the apodization effects along the propagation axis. Our method, based on discrete superpositions of Bessel-Gauss beams, enables the construction of finite versions of frozen waves, which is more suitable for predicting an experimental situation. Applications include optical trapping displays, continuous-depth holography, augmented and virtual reality, 3D printing systems, and so on.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband (UWB) Microstrip Bandstop Filter with Transmission Zeros
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-wideband (UWB) microstrip bandstop filter is proposed. The proposed bandstop filter is constructed with three open-circuited stubs separated by two quarter-wavelength transmission line sections. To enable the filter to exhibit very high selectivity, the electrical lengths of the first and third open-circuited stubs are designed to be half-wavelength long, while the electrical length of the second open-circuited stub is chosen to be a quarter-wavelength at the mid-band frequency. The filter is successfully designed, simulated, fabricated, and measured. The fabricated filter demonstrates excellent performance with a fractional bandwidth of more than 130% at the center frequency, exhibiting excellent agreement between the theoretical, simulated, and measured performance.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Metainspired Resonators for Copper Sensing in Water Bodies
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This work intends to observe the simulated response, based on experimental data, of three proposed sensors aiming to identify different concentrations of copper in water samples, as the MUT. Initially, solutions of distilled water, with 99.6% purity metallic copper powder, were prepared at concentrations of 0 mg/L, 8 mg/L and 10 mg/L. With the difference of resonance frequencies presented by each one of solutions on reflection coefficient, there was defined the frequency shifts analysis. The sensors were considered more sensitive according to the values of frequencies shifts. There were designed three types of sensors: a CSRR with a FR4 substrate, two SCRC - based with FR4 substrate and a CSRR with a PLA substrate. The last one presented almost 400 MHz by varying the concentration from 0 mg/L to 10 mg/L.

articleTitle: Detection of Broken Rotor Bar Defect Using Optical Fiber Bragg Grating Sensor and Terfenol-D Composite
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This work presents the fabrication and characterization of two magnetostrictive sensors based on fiber Bragg gratings (FBG) and magnetostrictive composites. The magnetostrictive composites were made by mixing Terfenol-D powder with epoxy resin and, during curing, the magnetic domains of one of the composites were oriented in order to determine the effects of orientation on the performance of the sensors. Once the magnetostrictive sensors were obtained, they were characterized with a DC magnetic field to evaluate their performance. The results revealed that the sensor with oriented magnetic domains had an increase in sensitivity of approximately 35% when compared to the non-oriented sensor. After determining the best sensor, it was placed inside a previously modified 2.2kW motor (with a broken bar) and subsequently in a healthy motor. The results demonstrated that the sensor was able to determine which of the motors had a bar break.

articleTitle: Uplink Performance of Massive LoRaWAN
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: In this paper, the performance of the uplink of a LoRaWAN for massive large-scale applications is presented considering different operation configurations and taking into account the radiopropagation characteristics of the region under study. The resulting developed model allows obtaining valuable information in the design of massive networks.

articleTitle: Analysis of a Switched Passive Input Network Based on a Surface Acoustic Wave Resonator for 433 MHz Wakeup Receivers
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: A switched passive input network (SPIN) for 433 MHz ISM band wakeup receivers with on-off keying (OOK) is discussed. It is based on a surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonator which is operated in a switched mode. The signal energy accumulated in the SAW resonator during a charge period appears as a voltage pulse, exhibiting up to 24 dB (measured) voltage gain referred to the open-circuit antenna port voltage. Input signal and noise are narrowband band-pass filtered with 364 kHz bandwidth (measured), which is favourable compared to conventional input matching networks in the crowded 433 MHz ISM band. In this paper, we present an analytical expression for the transient voltage at the switched passive input network for arbitrary parallel resistances. The passive voltage gain is calculated and compared to simulation results and measurements of a trial system.

articleTitle: Optical Fiber Sensor for Micro Displacement Monitoring Based on a Balloon-Like Interferometer with a Spring-Shaped Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: Ahstract-A sensor based on a balloon-like interferometer and a spring-shaped structure for micro curvature measurement is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. The sensor is composed by singlemode fiber inserted into a capillary tube. The experimental results show micro-curvature sensitivities of -35.04 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{pm}/\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>, -28.07 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{pm}/\mu \mathrm{m} \mathrm{e}-18.7 \text{pn}/\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> in the range from 0 to 200 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> for three resonants dips <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{1}, \lambda_{2}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{3}$</tex>, respectively. In addition, the sensor has advantages of easy fabrication, low cost, and satisfactory sensitivity, which shows good results of sensing of micro curvature in some applications.

articleTitle: Cost Minimization on OTN Interfaces: An ILP-Based Planning Model
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This paper introduces a practical approach to optimize Optical Transport Networks (OTNs) interfaces by the proposal of an Integer Linear Programming (ILP) mathematical model. The presented model focuses on minimizing the number of deployed OTN interfaces, the most costly element in the network, to reduce operational costs while meeting the aggregate traffic requirements. It considers various factors such as the network topology, different classes for the traffic demands, distinct-capacity interfaces and resource constraints. Extensive simulations were conducted and demonstrated the model's ability to find optimal solutions within short computation times, thereby improving resource utilization in the network.

articleTitle: Surface Enhanced Raman Scattering Properties of Titanium Nitride Films on Black Silicon Substrates
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: Titanium nitride (TiN) nanostructures were manufactured by depositing a thin film on a needle shaped structure of black silicon. The resulting TiN needle structure was characterized by scanning electron microscopy and UV-vis spectroscopy. The surface enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) properties of the created substrate was assessed using a probe molecule (Rhodamine 6G) showing strong enhancement of the original Raman signal on the order of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The created TiN surfaces showed to have promising Raman enhancement properties to create SERS substrates for sensing applications and being alternative for the most used materials such as gold or silver.

articleTitle: Generalization Evaluation of a Nonlinear Auto-Regressive Neural Network for PON Technologies
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)

authors.preferredName: Enzo Gomes Pinto Perin da Cruz

abstract: Building robust models with high generalization capability that can efficiently solve problems in a wide range of situations is essential to promote the development of enabling technologies. In this context, this paper evaluates the generalization capacity of a nonlinear autoregressive with external input neural network (NARXNET) for a passive optical network (PON). We adopted this type of neural network, given its applicability for nonlinear filtering processes, in which the target output is a noise-free version of the input signal. The built NARXNET was assessed with eight extra distinct experimental data sets demonstrating average RMSE and R2 values of 0.295 and 0.961, respectively, with a high generalization capability. Furthermore, NARXNET showed a fast training time of 240 seconds and an improved eye diagram for on-off keying (OOK) modulation format on a PON system.

articleTitle: Design of a Mach-Zehnder Modulator Using Silicon-on-Insulator Technology and Its Application in Opto-Electronic Oscillators
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: In this paper, the design of a Mach-Zehnder modulator (MZM) is presented. The MZM consists of the following building blocks: Phase-shifters based on the carrier injection principle, compact Y-branches, and waveguide bends. Each block was individually characterized at the device-level, and the performance of the modulator was evaluated through circuit-level simulation. Furthermore, we propose an application of the MZM in an opto-electronic oscillator (OEO) and verify its functionality within the OEO system.

articleTitle: Scattering Analysis by MoM of Continuous and Single Layer IRS with Variable Surface Impedance
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This paper presents a scattering model for an Intelligent Reflective Surface (IRS) with single and continuous layer by Method of Moments (MoM). We control the main beam using surface impedance with a progressive phase in one direction as the conventional array factor theory. Numerical results demonstrate the active and passive beamforming of a square IRS, with a side length of 5 wavelengths, operating at a frequency of 3.3GHz, and illuminated by a normally incident plane wave. Some results are compared with the commercial software CST Studio Suite and the array factor method and a good agreement was observed.

articleTitle: Firat Fractal Applied as Miniaturization Technique on Rectangular Microstrip Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: In this study, for the first time, Firat fractal pattern is applied to microstrip patch antenna design aiming to investigate its miniaturization potential. Previous study provided promising simulated data, which encouraged the authors to manufacture and characterize classic, rectangular microstrip patch antennas, as well as respective samples with iterations of the Firat fractal pattern. Reflection coefficient parameter presented a left-shift on resonance frequency up to 790 MHz, more expressive in the first-iteration samples. Resonance frequencies were used to design standard antennas and compare dimensions to estimate the miniaturization factor of each case, which led to values up to 62.02 %. Simulations were validated with good matching measured results, with maximum difference below 5.0 % for resonance frequencies.

articleTitle: Detection of Through-Wall Human Movement Using Ultra-Wideband Radar Technology: An Experimental Study
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: A 5 to 11 GHz ultra-wideband radar is presented to visualize human presence behind walls, following indoor measurements. The raw backscattered data is analyzed using two different techniques to identify human movement, one based in subtraction and other using Moving Target Indicator filtering. The radar was found to be sensitive enough to detect human movements behind a wall, in three different indoor scenarios. Signal to noise ratio analyzes are implemented to evaluate the generated image after the processing.

articleTitle: Diesel Adulteration Sensor Based on D-Shaped Optical Fiber
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: Combustion engines are indispensable components for various applications, such as vehicle propulsion or power generators. These components have been the subject of research aimed mainly at increasing their efficiency and reducing emissions of air pollutants, but despite these efforts, these devices still suffer from fuel adulteration. This practice significantly reduces the useful life-time of engines and results in several social, economic and environmental problems ranging from unfair competition to increased emissions. From this scenario, this work proposes a sensor to detect kerosene mixed with diesel, a common adulteration in several countries due to the economic importance of diesel and the low price of kerosene. The proposed sensor is based on D-shaped optical fiber and the fabrication process is also presented.

articleTitle: Plasmonic Resonances Associated with Distinct Conducting Layers Deposited on a D-Shaped Photonic Crystal Fiber: An Analysis for Sensing Purpose
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: The spectral response of a SPR (surface plasmon resonance) sensor depends on the engineering of the conducting layer. In this paper, we analyze theoretically the spectra of a D-shaped SPR PCF (photonic crystal fiber) refractive index sensor considering four different plasmonic materials: Ag, Au, Ga-doped zinc oxide (GZO) and an Ag-nanowire metamaterial. The sensing properties provided by each material and how they form the bases to design multiplasmonic resonance sensors are the focus of our discussion.

articleTitle: Dual Polarized Patch Antenna Array with Capacitive Proximity Sensor for Hand Grip Detection in 5G mmWave Mobile Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: We propose a novel dual polarized patch antenna array with a capacitive proximity sensor function for detecting the user's hand on 5G millimeter-wave mobile devices. The proposed antenna array consists of eight proximity-coupled-fed patch elements that generate dual polarized waves. Each element is composed of one radiating patch, two orthogonal proximity-coupled feeds, and a ground plane. The patch also serves as a proximity sensor by using the capacitance change of the patch that occurs when the user's hand approaches the patch. The proposed antenna array is designed to operate in the 5G n257 band (26.5 to 29.5 GHz). The simulation results show a stable gain of 13.6-14.0 dBi in the 5G n257 band and a cross-polarization of below -23 dB at 28 GHz. It is also shown that each array element can act as a capacitive proximity sensor that exhibits a 100 fF capacitance change upon hand proximity.

articleTitle: Investigation of a K-Band SiGe VCO for FMCW Radar Localization
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: The design and characterization of a 24 GHz LC cross-coupled voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) for a frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) primary radar for automotive applications is presented. To prove the concept, the VCO is fabricated using 130 nm SiGe technology. The studied VCO is measured both on wafer and printed circuit board (PCB). It consumes 7.2 mA from a 2.5 V supply, has an efficiency of 1.48 GHz/mW, and features a tuning range of 12%. The measured phase noise on PCB is -103 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz offset frequency. To our knowledge, compared to the state-of-the-art, the circuit shows the highest figure of merit tuning range (FOMT) of -180 dBc/Hz for LC cross-coupled VCOs.

articleTitle: Planar Wide-Band MIMO Antenna using a Modified EBG Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: A planar MIMO antenna using a modified EBG structure to increase bandwidth is proposed in this work. The antenna is printed on a Rogers RT-5880 dielectric substrate with a 40 × 20 x 0.787 mm size. Two hexagonal patch antennas in a MIMO array are placed in front of an EBG structure. The EBG structure is made using an array of 4 by 4 cells. Each cell resonates at 8 GHz. The measurement shows that the antenna operates over a bandwidth of7.3 GHz GHz (3.69 to 10.99 GHz) with a maximum gain of 10.4 dBi. The EBG structure improved the gain and the radiation pattern. A Good agreement between simulations and measurements was obtained. The proposed antenna could be used for ISM, 5G, IoT, and S-Band (radar and Satellite) applications.

articleTitle: Rapid Toxicological Tests Using Algae Luminescence
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: The delayed luminescence of algae samples (Raphidocelis subcapitata) is used to infer the toxicity of ametryn solutions, as well as for a preliminary sensitivity tests with salt (NaCl). For both substances, consistent results appear just 1 hour after inoculation, confirming the reproducibility of such photonic tests that save consumable materials and workforce and present dose x response plots similar to those obtained by the standard growth, 72-h long tests.

articleTitle: ANN-based LiDAR Positioning System for B5G
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: Accurate positioning and mapping are essential in telecommunications applications, but conventional methods, including the Global Positioning System (GPS), have limitations in indoor environments. This paper presents preliminary results on the effectiveness of using Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) for indoor positioning, specifically targeting beyond 5G (B5G) applications, with a focus on the integration of LiDAR in these networks. The proposed system utilizes a two-dimensional LiDAR sensor for data acquisition and digital filters for signal improvement. The proposed methodology involves object detection using LiDAR and camera fusion, employing an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) for people detection. We demonstrate person detection within a designated area, by harnessing the complementary strengths of LiDAR and camera technologies.

articleTitle: Preprocessing Algorithm for Seismic Signals Monitored by Fiber Optic Distributed Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: Fiber optic-based sensors have experimented with significant technological advances in the last two decades. Distributed acoustic sensors represent their most recent iteration. This sensing technology become all the cable length into a sensor, a favorable condition for seismic studies. Data preprocessing is a crucial step in this study, in which the seismic signals captured by optical interrogators must be converted to the apparent velocity of particles that sensitized the fiber. Amongst the main conversion algorithms, the ones based on Fourier Transforms are more adopted at large-scale surveys. This paper presents an algorithm implementation for this conversion, based on the 2D Fourier Transform, in a small-scale laboratory investigation. The results are favorable and show that it is a possible use. It brings more definition to individualizing first break time arrivals, equalizing signal amplitude, and aligning oscillation peaks, essential parameters for applying reflections and refraction methods in seismic studies.

articleTitle: In-Vehicle Monitoring Based on a Low-Cost mm-Wave Radar at 60 GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This work presents an in-vehicle monitoring system based on a PCR (Pulsed Coherent Radar) at the 60 GHz ISM unlicensed band. The radar can measure distances with sub-millimeter resolution. Therefore, a detection system has been designed for both seat occupancy and people's breathing monitoring since the radar has the capacity to measure displacements of the order of mm. The results of the respiration measurement agree with those obtained by another system whose measurements are based on the airflow, which allows its validation In addition, a proof-of-concept of gesture recognition based on the same radar is proposed.

articleTitle: Neural Network Surrogate Modeling of a Synthetic Bi-Physical Second Order Low-Pass Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: In this work, an initial step forward to address the development of multi-physics neural modeling is presented. The initial step consists of a prove of concept to determine if a neural network model (NN) is enough accurate to represent the bi-physical response (electrical and thermal) of a second order low-pass filter. Three different learning algorithms were used to train the neural network, being the Bayesian Regularization the model which exhibits the best generalization performance to represent the EM responses subject to changes in the circuit temperature.

articleTitle: Impedance Matching Prediction and Optimization of Yagi-Uda Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This work presents the development of a methodology that allows accurate impedance matching estimation of a Yagi-Uda antenna using a Multilayer Perceptron artificial neural network. Additionally, results of dimensions that minimize the reflection coefficient are presented. These dimensions were defined using the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithms multi-objective optimization algorithm. The ANSYS HFSS simulation software is utilized to generate the artificial neural network database and also to validate the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Propagation of Uncertainty in Data-Driven Models Used for Long-Period Fiber Grating Interrogation
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: The use of machine learning (ML) for processing fiber optic sensors (FOS) signals has several advantages. Some ML models have great data abstraction capability, thus allowing data interpolation and/or extrapolation. Thus, it enables the interrogation of long-period fiber grating (LPFG) sensors using a sparse filter array. In this case, an array of optical powers filtered by the filter array is processed by the ML model to estimate the LPFG resonance. This setup provides great scalability, because it is sensor-independent, i.e., there is no need for the interrogator to be calibrated for each LPFG. In this work we present a study on the uncertainty propagation in such interrogation scheme.

articleTitle: Optimization of the Surface Plasmon Resonance Effect on a Rectangular Metal Grating
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: In this work, the particle swarm optimization algorithm is used to determine the optimum parameters for maximum sensitivity of the surface plasmon resonance effect at normal incidence on a rectangular metal grating. To avoid convergence problems, a continuous function is used to represent the grating profile. For the optimization problem, the Rayleigh's hypothesis is used to model the diffracted fields across a metal-vacuum interface. The calculated responses, obtained by use of either the more rigorous Chandezon method or COMSOL's finite element based approach, confirm the validity of the optimization approach.

articleTitle: Ag Ink-Jet Printed CPW with Micro-Surface Cavities: Effects of Cavity Removal on RF Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This paper presents a study on the RF characteristics of CPW transmission lines with micro-surface cavities generated by Ag ink-jet printing. The cavities were formed by printing Ag ink on a substrate and then drying the ink. The size and number of cavities changed depending on the drying temperature. The RF characteristics of the transmission lines were measured using a vector network analyzer. The insertion loss at 3 GHz was measured to be 0.046 dB/mm at 30°C, 0.043 dB/mm at 65°C, and 0.039 dB/mm at 100°C. The results show that the presence of the cavities degrades the RF characteristics of the transmission lines, particularly at high frequencies.

articleTitle: Advancing Innovation in Photonic Technologies at a Brazilian Research and Development Center
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: Photonics plays a crucial role in advancing various technologies, especially in supporting future optical communication networks. This paper presents some of the challenges and developments being carried out in Brazil, specifically at CPQD, a Brazilian research and development center in telecommunications. We present CPQD's capabilities in integrated photonics, highlight results from projects in the field, and discuss the Sisfáton initiative, emphasizing the importance of funding and collaborations to foster innovations in the field.

articleTitle: New Configuration for Ultra-Wideband (UWB) Bandpass Filter with Notch
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: In this paper, a parallel-coupled line microstrip bandpass filter with an ultra-wideband (UWB) passband and a narrow notched band is presented. The proposed UWB microstrip bandpass filter is constructed of one section of three parallel-coupled line that is a quarter-wavelength long at the center frequency. The filter is designed to have a very wideband passband with a fractional bandwidth of %110 at a center frequency of 6.85 GHz. In order to enhance the filter selectivity, the middle line is extended by a length of quarter-wavelength and shorted to the ground at the end. Therefore, a single transmission zero is generated at each edge of the desired UWB passband which enhances the filter performance. Furthermore, an embedded open circuited stub is implemented to generate a narrow notched band inside the UWB passband for blocking unwanted existing radio signal. The filter design is verified by simulation and experiment where excellent agreement is obtained. The fabricated filter is very compact in size and has very low insertion loss.

articleTitle: 4-BIT FSS Based IFM System Using Balanced Binary Code
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This article presents four Frequency Selective Surfaces (FSS) with double square loops geometry to be used in an Instantaneous Frequency Measurement (IFM) system. The proposed FSSs have a frequency response based on balanced Gray code, corresponding to the characteristics of frequency discriminators. Unlike traditional Gray code, it is possible to use only dual-band resonators instead of quadriband, simplifying the system and improving the response. A 4-bit IFM system is shown with a resolution of approximately 140 MHz, containing 16 distinct frequency sub-bands between 0.7 and 3 GHz. Finally, spectral occupancy levels are measured in the upper UHF frequency range to verify the applicability of the proposed system. Simulations in CST software and measurements of insertion parameters are presented and compared with.

articleTitle: Mobile Channel Multipath Measurements and Statistical Characterization in Sub-6 GHz Bands
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This paper compares mobile wideband channel characteristics obtained from measurements performed at 735 MHz, 2.5 GHz, and 3.5 GHz in urban environments in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Both macrocell and microcell scenarios were considered. To characterize the macrocell channel, the transmitter antenna was installed high above the ground, with the receiver antenna and equipment in an automotive van ran along routes up to 1.5 km from the transmitter. The transmitter antenna was installed on a 3m pole for the microcell measurements, and the van with the receiver equipment moved along a few hundred meters paths. Multipath power delay profiles were obtained using an OFDM sounding technique and processed to provide average excess delay and RMS delay spread values. Also, the cumulative distributions of the RMS delay spread were obtained.

articleTitle: Power Transmission at 113 MHz Using Universal Software Radio Peripheral and GNU Radio
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)

authors.preferredName: João P. S. B. Da Silva

abstract: Software-defined radio requires a combination of software-based signal processing and enabling hardware components. This article uses software-defined radio to study an energy transmission system at the frequency of 113 MHz. The relationship between the transmitted and received power was obtained experimentally using telescopic antennas of 54 cm separated at distances of 20, 30, and 40 cm. It was possible to validate the linear relationship between the powers using the Friis equation.

articleTitle: A Comparison of DGT and Power Mask for EDFA Modeling in GNPy
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: EDFAs (erbium-doped fiber amplifiers) are essential equipment in optical networks. In addition to enabling trans-mission over long distances in the all-optical domain, EDFAs amplify several optical spectrum channels. An intrinsic problem with EDFAs is that the channels are not equally amplified, with variation in gain along the spectrum according to the chosen operating point. This problem can considerably impair the transmitted signal in a cascade of amplifiers. How the amplifier characteristics and operation are represented is critical to predicting the signal quality at the end of the link. This paper compares two strategies for representing optical amplifier operation: DGT (Dynamic Gain Tilt) and Power Mask. We perform simulations using the GNPY library and two commercial EDFA models. The results indicate that the DGT estimation is worse when the amplifier has a high ripple operating point, reaching a 13 dB difference in the output power spectrum at the end of a link with 4 EDFAs.

articleTitle: Scintillation Effects in High Energy Laser Propagation: A Numerical Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: A modeling of a laser beam propagation through the atmosphere has been developed and is reported in this paper. The effects of scintillation are numerically simulated in a coupled numerical solution. This solution has been done by using Navier-Stokes. paraxial euuations and a phase-screen model.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Investigation of Laser Frequency Noise Characteristics Using Self-Homodyne Setup and Computational Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: Our study presents a technique for analyzing frequency noise in semiconductor lasers using a self-homodyne method. Through the application of a computational approach to experimental data, we identify different types of noise by calculating their respective areas, including Lorentzian, Gaussian, and excess noise. The findings of our investigation revealed that as the laser emission power decreases, the white phase noise (Lorentzian line shape) diminishes both in quantity and proportion. Consequently, the contributions of non-Lorentzian noise components, resulting from environmental and technical factors (Gaussian line shape) as well as excess noise, become more pronounced.

articleTitle: Optimizing a Fast Fourier Transform Algorithm Implemented with Integer Arithmetic
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: Digital signal processing fixed-point arithmetic is widely adopted because of its lower execution cost than that of floating-point arithmetic. Since defining the number of bits (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$NBW$</tex>) of fixed-points variables and its integer part (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$NBI$</tex>) representation can be time consuming, a simulation-based tool for optimizing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$NBW$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$NBI$</tex> is proposed. Its performance is evaluated for the 256-point Radix-2 Fast Fourier Transform algorithm. The results suggest that the evolutionary optimization step for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$NBW$</tex> can be skipped when dealing with linear transformation algorithms, reducing the number of simulations required and, therefore, speeding up the tool.

articleTitle: Bandpass Filter Using Open Loop Microstrip Resonators for a Power Substation Eyebolt Fault Detection System
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)

authors.preferredName: José M. A M. De Oliveira
Lauro R. G. S. Lourenço Novo

abstract: Eyebolts are metal parts used to support mechanical efforts of heavy structures. These eyebolts may present material loss, either through abrasion or corrosive processes on their surface. Detecting this undesirable condition requires the use of systems which applies non-destructive techniques, since the eyebolt is embedded in concrete. A previous detection system was developed by the authors where its response requires greater sensitivity. This article presents the computational design of a band-pass filter from a microstrip resonator to reduce mismatching losses at the experiment input and the measuring instrument. The designed filter has presented satisfactory results as an adapter for the fault detection system. The simulation results of the fault detection system has presented different responses for distinct eyebolt samples, and thus enabling the desired classifying of them.

articleTitle: ITO-Silver SPR Single-Channel Dual Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: An optical fiber surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensor is proposed for simultaneous temperature and refractive index (RI) measurements. The sensor utilizes a multimode fiber coated with a thin metal layer of ITO and Ag. The sensor produces two wavelength dips, due to SPR and lossy mode resonance (LMR), that changes linearly with temperature and RI. The second dip is utilized to achieve higher accuracy and solve the cross-sensitivity issue. The sensor has RI sensitivities of 2,586 nm/RIU and 194.4 nm/RIU, and temperature sensitivities of -31.72 pm/K and -13.49 pm/K, respectively.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized MIMO Antenna with Band-Notched Characteristic for UWB Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This work presents a miniaturized multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna for ultrawideband (UWB) applications with band-notched characteristic. The MIMO antenna prototype presents a compact size of 18 mm x 32 mm and a high isolation above 16 dB is achieved between the antenna elements over entire UWB band. F-shaped stubs are introduced in the ground plane to improve isolation between the radiating elements. Double L-shaped parasitic element is introduced between the antenna ports to improve isolation and enhance the antenna bandwidth. Furthermore, Z-shaped slits were etched on the MIMO antenna patches to generate a band notch at the WLAN band (5.15 to 5.825 GHz). Simulations were performed in Ansoft HFSS software, for numerical characterization, and the prototype was fabricated and measured, presenting a good agreement between simulated and measured results. Moreover, the envelope correlation coefficient (ECC), which is a key performance parameter in MIMO antennas, is investigated and presents good results.

articleTitle: Design of Millimeter-Wave Broadband Antenna Array with hand-grip sensing for 5G mobile
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: We propose the millimeter-wave broadband 1 × 8 antenna array with user hand grip sensing functionality for mobile application. The built-in device is called “SENTENNA” which stands for SENsor and anTENNA. The proposed antenna has the structure of a double patches array and a two per-pendicularly T-sharped proximity-coupled fed patch for dual polarizations. The proximity-coupled square microstrip patch antenna array of SENTENNA is designed and simulated to operate at the entire global mm-wave 5G spectrum band and capacitance variation on the patch is analyzed at 1 MHz. The performance of the designed SENTENNA is evaluated by HFSS simulation.

articleTitle: Analysis of Exposure to Electromagnetic Fields Due to Multiple Sources in a Classroom Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of the electromagnetic fields (EMF) exposure to multiple sources in a classroom environment. The research is motivated by the increasing use of electronic devices in educational environments and the need to estimate this. The methodology used involves simulating a classroom with students using laptops, which are considered as the main sources of electromagnetic radiation. The 1g and 10 g peak spacial Specific Absorption Rate (psSAR) are calculated for different parts of the human body, including the head, back, and hands. The results indicate that the psSAR is higher in the back, followed by the head and hands. When the free distance between desks is 250 mm, two-fold at the hands to forty-five-fold at the back greater psSAR are obtained when comparing to just one student with his laptop.

articleTitle: Passive and Flexible UHF RFID Tag for Body-Worn Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: There is a great interest in epidermal devices that provide comfort to users. In this work, an RFID tag for on-body applications on a polyimide substrate was proposed. The tag consists of a low-profile flexible substrate that conforms to the body's curvature, allowing comfortable monitoring of physiological functions. The passive tag has a total dimension of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$112.6\times 26.6\ \text{mm}^{2}$</tex>. It is composed of a folded dipole antenna, in which two Complementary Split Ring Resonator (CSRR) cells were incorporated to improve its performance in proximity to the body, and the Monza® X-2K Dura chip from Impinj®. According to the simulation results, its maximum read range is 3.21 m. Two experiments were carried out: one without the presence of the human body and another with the tag on the abdomen of a volunteer. The maximum read range achieved in the first configuration was 1.89 m, and in the second configuration, it was 1.10 m.

articleTitle: Hybrid Integration of Polymer PICs and InP Optoelectronics for WDM and SDM Terabit Intra-DC Optical Interconnects
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This paper presents a hybrid photonic integration concept based on the use of a polymer motherboard, InP EML arrays and InP PD arrays to realize WDM and SDM Terabit optical engines operating at 100-Gb/s or even at 200-Gb/s per lane. The optical engines are aligned with the Ethernet roadmap, are cost-efficient by design and can find their place in the next generation Terabit IM/DD optical transceivers within Data Centers.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of an Ultra-Wideband Polarization Converter Based on Anisotropic Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)

authors.preferredName: Antônio Luiz Pereira De Siqueira Campos

abstract: A metasurface-based ultrathin and ultrawideband reflective linear polarization converter is designed and simulated in this research. Through three resonances generated in a periodic array composed of a circular patch cut at 45 degrees and two square slits, a bandwidth expansion is obtained, making it possible to cover almost completely the X-band, entirely the Ku-band and partially the K-band. Simulation results show that the metasurface converts linearly polarized waves into cross polarized waves from 8.32 to 21.82 GHz, with a total bandwidth greater than 13 GHz. Furthermore, efficient cross-polarization conversion is achieved with fractional -10 dB bandwidth of nearly 90% with an average polarization conversion rate of 97%. The proposed cross-polarization converter (CPC) is λ/12.8 in thickness and λ/4.5 in periodicity at the lowest frequency.

articleTitle: Substrate-Integrated Waveguide Fed Coplanar Printed Phased Array Antenna Mounted on FR-4
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: A three-by-one coplanar phased array antenna built on a Flame Retardant Fiberglass Epoxy (FR-4) substrate is designed for ~ 10 GHz wireless communication, satellite communication, or radar systems. Simulation results point to 70° aperture at 9.88GHz, with a -10dB bandwidth of 600 MHz.

articleTitle: Spatiotemporal Dynamics of Eletctromagnetic Waves in Resonator with Nonlinearly Reflecting Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: One-dimensional electromagnetic (EM) resonator, formed by a thin semi-transparent metasurface layer with a nonlinear reflectivity has been studied theoretically. This system may serve as a simplest model of many electronic and electromagnetic devices in the microwave, terahertz, and optical frequency ranges. A metasurface may be placed at the arbitrary point inside the above resonator or at its semitransparent wall. Initial-Boundary value problem for linear wave equation with nonlinear boundary conditions was formulated and reduced to the simpler Cauchy problem for system of two functional equations with deviated argument. A nonlinear transformation of the partial EM waves by the nonlinear metasurface takes place, and the spatiotemporal dynamics of the waves may be either a simple standing wave or may have a very complicated, but still deterministic, behavior. Finally, the wave dynamics in the resonator with active metasurface may be a stochastic one.

articleTitle: Preliminary Results of the Indoor Coverage Field Tests of the Advanced ISDB-T System in Brazil
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This article presents the preliminary results of field tests with the Advanced Integrated Services Digital Broadcasting for Terrestrial Television Broadcasting (ISDB- T) system in indoor environments. Received channel power and error-free system reception threshold records were performed at four different measurement sites. Five different H/V dual-polarized MIMO antennas are used in measurements to evaluate system performance when using antennas from different manufacturers. The results show that the advanced ISDB-T system is robust to indoor penetration losses and when subjected to the use of different antennas.

articleTitle: A Novel Technique for Open Stop Band Suppression in 1-D Combline LWA Using Slots
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: A design of a 1-D PLWA is discussed where a slot is introduced in the structure to suppress an open stop band, obtain broadside scanning, and reduce gain variation at broadside frequency [10GHz]. A slot is introduced in a rectangular stub with an offset from the centerline which is further connected to a microstrip fed line. The proposed antenna can achieve 15.75dBi peak gain and have a scanning range from −52° to +12°, bandwidth 6.85GHz −11.35GHz, its dimensions are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8.72\lambda_{0}\times 1.33\lambda_{0}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Design of Reflective Coding Metasurface for Terahertz Wave Beam Steering for 6G Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: Optical beam steering is needed in many applications such as LIDAR, 6G communications, laser machining, and 3D printing. In this paper, we report the design of a reflective coding metasurface for 0.3 THz beam steering. The unit cell is designed to operate as a 3-bit coding metasurface to achieve better control of EM waves. The proposed 3-bit coding metasurfaces can reflect the incident EM wave with a high reflection angle up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$77.5^{o}$</tex>, which is in good agreement with the theoretical prediction. The obtained results show that the proposed coding metasurface is a suitable candidate for THz wave beam steering for 6G technology.

articleTitle: Quantum Key Distribution in Optical Fibers: A Comprehensive View Beyond Transmission
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This paper reports a network operator point of view about the introduction of Quantum Key Distribution in optical networks to secure the data plane and/or specific applications, focusing on the aspects that go beyond pure transmission.

articleTitle: Antennas and Electromagnetic Propagation Aspects for Drone-Borne Synthetic Aperture Radars
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: Drone-borne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) is becoming a powerful remote sensing tool for subsoil tomography. Two challenging aspects need to be considered: the development of processing techniques for complex subsoil tomography tasks and the reduction in volume and weight of the SAR system. These challenges will be addressed through two key applications. The first aspect will be exemplified by describing the identification of ant nests in the subsoil of an industrial forest using an electromagnetic-based P-band SAR approach. The second will be tackled by presenting the optimized design of an L-band polarimetric conformal antenna.

articleTitle: Current Sensing Through an Optical Sensor Based on an Etched Side-Hollow Fiber Interferometer and Terfenol-D
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This work presents a current sensor based on an in-fiber interferometer and Terfenol-D. The in-fiber interferometer was fabricated by etching the tip of a single-mode optical fiber (doped with germanium in its core) using hydrofluoric acid. After etching, the etched optical fiber was fused with another unetched fiber, resulting in a junction between the two fibers with a hollow region. This configuration created a Fabry-Perot interferometer within the optical fiber. After manufacturing the sensor, it was affixed to a piece of Terfenol-D using adhesive. Subsequently, the sensor underwent characterization with a DC magnetic field and an AC current ranging from 100 A to 800 A. The results showed that the sensor exhibited a sensitivity to a DC magnetic field of 8.5 pm/mT and a sensitivity of 35.8 1–1V/Arms for AC current. This sensitivity was found to be three times higher than that of a commercial Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) sensor.

articleTitle: AI-driven Maintenance Tool for Synchronous Power Generator Temperature Monitoring Using Fiber Bragg Gratings
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: The carbon brushes and slip rings of a hydrogen-erator are the main components guiding the excitation current from the bridge to the rotor windings. The brushes' temperature are crucial to infer their operational condition and, the generator status. This work presents the temperature measurement of six Fiber Bragg Gratings (FBG) sensors installed in a 370 MVA electric generator brushes. The results show the sensors' capacity to monitor the brushes' temperature in accordance with the current flowing through them. Together with the sensors, an Artificial Intelligence (AI) technique was applied to the measured temperature to detect anomalous events regarding the current supplied to the rotor windings. The optical sensors combined with the AI could detect five events of abnormal current behaviour. One is presented in detail in this paper. This sensing system can be further applied to online fault detection using the temperature measured by the FBGs as a brush condition indicator and a generator operation and maintenance tool.

articleTitle: Microcontrolled Lock-In Amplifier for Spectroscopy Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)

authors.preferredName: Bernardo Caio Nunes De Oliveira Lima

abstract: This article describes the development of a dedicated microcontrolled digital lock-in amplifier based on an STM32 microcontroller chip. The prototype was used in experiments of wavelength modulation spectroscopy, directed to the detection of acetylene in a multiple-pass spectrometric cell having 78 cm of optical path length. Paired experiments were done with a commercial DSP7265 lock-in amplifier. A strong correlation between measurements was observed in general for varying concentration of acetylene, with a minimum correlation of 95% observed for the lowest acetylene concentration detected at 13 ppm.

articleTitle: Highly-Sensitive Microwave Phase-Variation Permittivity Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This paper summarizes the recent progress in reflective-mode phase-variation permittivity sensors carried out by the authors and emphasizes the main strategies for sensitivity optimization. It is also shown that losses might help to boost up the sensitivity provided the sensor is adequately designed.

articleTitle: Design of a Simplified 1-Bit Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface for ISM Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces are arrays capable of anomalously reflecting electromagnetic waves due to modifying the reflected wave phase controlled by switching devices. This new technology has been studied based on reconfigurable reflect arrays and metasurfaces for the introduction of its use in the Fifth and Sixth generations of mobile networks. So in this work, we design a 1-bit reconfigurable intelligent surface capable of modifying the beamforming reflected on its surface controlled at 2.45 GHz by commercial PIN diodes. Simulations carried out by ANSYS HFSS demonstrated that the structure generated two switching states shifted by one hundred and eighty degrees and modified the reflected beam anomalously in a array of one hundred elements.

articleTitle: Design of a 915 MHz SWIPT Integrated Receiver Based on Intermodulated Signals
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This work proposes an easy-to-implement Simulta-neous Wireless Information and Power Transfer receiver based on intermodulated signals. Operating at 915 MHz ISM band, it starts from the standalone Energy Harvesting (EH) design thus, developing an Information Decoding (ID) block for rectifying only the intermodulation components. Simulations demonstrated a good agreement of the ID performance with the BFSK-IM modulation for input powers above -20 dBm, and the ID block could have minimal impact on the EH performance.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Practical Coherent DSP Aspects on High-Baud Rate Submarine Systems Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: In this work, we numerically investigate the impact of digital signal processing (DSP) stack implementation aspects on submarine systems using DP-QPSK, DP-8QAM, and DP-16QAM at 90 GBd. Results for different fibers showed a significant performance degradation when the practical DSP aspects were considered, especially for higher-order modulation formats. The achieved results highlight the importance of a more thorough analysis when designing the DSP algorithms, especially for the next generation of high-capacity optical systems.

articleTitle: Interrogation Technique Using Harmonic Equations in the Electrical Domain for Long Period Grating Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This paper presents a new interrogation technique for Long Period Grating (LPG) sensors using harmonic equations. The technique is supported by the comparison of the harmonic equations with the measured harmonics, in the electrical domain.

articleTitle: Next-Generation Optical Transceiver and Switching Solutions Exploiting MB and SDM
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: Novel multiband (MB) and spatial division multiplexing (SDM) transceiver and node architectures, capable to exploit spectral (wavelength-band) and spatial dimensions, are presented as suitable options to target potential capacity scaling of future optical networks. A proof of concept assessment of the proposed transceiver is performed demonstrating MB (C+S)+SDM transmission after 19-cores MCF of 25.4 km.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Speeding Up the Min Slot-Continuity Capacity Loss Spectrum Assignment
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This paper presents two classifier models based on deep neural networks to speed up the Min Slot-Continuity Capacity Loss (MSCL) spectrum assignment. The first decides between the use of First-Fit or MSCL heuristic, with the aim of avoiding unnecessary MSCL calls whenever the application of First-Fit would provide the same minimum loss of capacity as MSCL. The second adds the capability of pointing out the correct portion of the spectrum MSCL should look for whenever First-Fit is not selected. Simulation results demonstrate reductions of 28% and 74% on the simulation time between the MSCL and the two proposed models without mitigation on the MSCL performance.

articleTitle: ZnO Nanoflake-Decorated Si Nanowire Photodiode with Enhanced Reponsivity
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: We report a Si nanowire photodiode decorated with ZnO nanoflakes for enhanced photoresponse. The photodiode consists of a core-shell Si nanowire array and ZnO nanoflakes and exhibits a higher responsivity than the Si nanowire photodiode. The improvement is achieved by decorating the nanowire array with ZnO nanoflakes. In addition, the responsivity increases slightly with applied reverse bias. Analysis of the reflectance and energy band diagram was performed in order to elucidate the enhancement mechanism. The higher responsivity is caused by reduced surface reflectance, which allows absorption of more light within the Si nanowire array.

articleTitle: CPU Usage Estimation for 5G UE by mmWave Carrier Aggregation
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: 5G networks bring a major advance in bandwidth extension through millimeter wave (mmWave). Previously impractical services such as enhanced mobile broadband (eMBB), ultra-reliable latency communications (URLCC), and machine type communications (mMTC) can be applied with QoS (Quality of Service) and QoE (Quality of Experience) for users connected to the network. Under mmWave, higher data rates are achieved with the multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) and carrier aggregation (CA), meeting several demands of the user. However, a significant increase in user equipment (UE) capabilities is required over very high data rates, reflecting extra CPU processing demands and battery consumption, which can reach critical levels faster with potential disconnection. Considering the CPU processing growth in UE over such a situation, this work presents an estimation model to obtain processing growth curves according to the network features on mm Wave. As a result, the obtained CPU monitoring functions can predict the longer battery life for UE data throughput demands.

articleTitle: RF Transversal Planar Filters With Dual-Lowpass/Bandpass Response
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: The optimization-based design of RF / microwave transversal signal-interference planar filters with composite-lowpass /bandpass transfer function is reported. As their basic constituent circuit stage, these filters exploit a transversal filtering section (TFS) composed of two stepped-impedance-transmission-line electrical paths. Thus, by means of constructive / destructive RF-signal-combination mechanisms taking place inside this class of bi-path TFS, sharp-rejection dual-lowpass/bandpass filtering responses with extended upper stopband can be realized. Higher-order designs with increased selectivity / out-of-band-attenuation levels can also be implemented by means of in-series-cascaded multi-TFS circuit arrangements. For experimental-demonstration purposes, two microstrip prototypes consisting of single- and two-TFS-based circuits are designed, fabricated, and characterized.

articleTitle: Leveraging Programmability of Photonic Devices Towards Agile and Autonomous Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: The emergence and consolidation of increasingly programmable optical devices (transceivers, amplifiers, multiplexers), which allow their remote configuration and control into multiple modes of operation, is enabling the evolution towards more autonomous networks. Such networks leverage this programmability and are able to adapt and react to traffic and network condition changes, paving the way for the increased adoption of AI/ML models in support of network operation. In this paper, we review key elements in the control and orchestration systems of optical networks in support of autonomous networking, including configuration and optical telemetry aspects and we present some uses cases focusing on our evolving prototype of sliceable bandwidth variable transceiver, focusing on the design of the SDN agent.

articleTitle: Refraction Effect in SAR Processing for Focused Subsurface Tomography
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: In synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging, the goal of subsurface tomography is to create detailed images of objects and structures underground. In order to obtain well-focused images, the refraction effect must be taken into account during SAR processing. This work proposes an adjusted back-projection algorithm and validates it with simulation and experimental results. The simulation model constitutes an underground air cavity and a multi-circular flight path. The experimental scenario includes a buried quad-corner reflector and an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) performing a spiral flight path. Both cases produced well-focused 3D images with the correct positioning of the targets.

articleTitle: Design and Characterization of a 50-GHz-Bandwidth IQ Modulator for High-Capacity Optical Transmissions
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This paper presents the design and experimental characterization of a silicon-on-insulator-based in-phase and quadrature electro-optical modulator with a bandwidth of 50 GHz. Electromagnetic simulations were carried out to focus on optimizing the trade-off between electro-optical bandwidth, extinction ratio, and insertion loss in order to meet the requirements for supporting 1 Tb/s optical transmissions. Experimental characterization demonstrated that the modulator's performance aligns closely with the optimization simulations and the requirements for the intended application.

articleTitle: Non-Uniform Phase Synthesis for Cosecant-Squared Radiation Patterns
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This work presents the development of an analytical technique for the synthesis of non-uniform phase distribution for a cylindrical aperture with a cosecant-squared radiation pattern. Analytical results for the phase distributions are presented. Using the Aperture Method, the radiation patterns for these distributions are computationally calculated.

articleTitle: Amplitude Only Direction of Arrival Estimation
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: In this manuscript, we present a novel hardware concept for the estimation of the direction of arrival of electro-magnetic signals. An arrangement of two patch antenna arrays, tilted with respect to each other, is used to create a monotonic relationship between the DoA and the received power difference between both arrays. The proof of concept is performed using numerical simulations, and we demonstrate that by maintaining the same boresight direction, but tilting the beam in relation to the propagation axis, DoA estimation through power difference can be achieved. The proposed technique aims to reduce the complexity of such estimation systems in the hardware, as well as in the digital signal processing domain, by removing the need for phase comparison.

articleTitle: A 3D-Printed Monolithic Inline Filter Fabricated With Titanium Alloy
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: The paper presents a 5th order bandpass filter for communication satellite feed systems, fabricated using 3D-printing with Titanium alloy Ti-6Al-4V or Ti64. Taking advantage of the alloy's high strength-to-weight ratio, the filter is printed with a wall thickness of only 1 mm and a weight of 40 g. Ti64 also has a much lower coefficient of thermal expansion than aluminium. The filter was designed with modified rectangular cavity resonators with rounded corners, enabling monolithic printing of the structure in a lying-down position without any internal supports. The coupling irises have been moved to one side of the filter to facilitate polishing and silver coating. The measured response of the as-printed filter showed a minimum insertion loss of 2.7 dB and a frequency shift of about 140 MHz. After silver plating, the insertion loss was significantly reduced to a minimum of 0.55 dB. The challenge with plating on the Ti64 filter has been discussed.

articleTitle: Semiconductor Optical Amplifiers in High Capacity Fiber Transmission
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: The fast gain dynamics of the semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA) can give rise to signal distortions in wavelength division multiplexing transmission. Two recent experiments show that high channel count and the use of forward error correction effectively combat this impairment, making the SOA a candidate for high capacity, long distance transmission systems.

articleTitle: Multifunctional Metasurface for Absorption, Polarization Conversion and Transmission
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: A metasurface generally has a single function, as they can only absorb incident energy and, in some cases, in addition to absorbing also transmit, or convert the polarization state of an incident wave. Bringing new breakthroughs, in this manuscript, a multifunctional thin metasurface is presented. The proposed structure is composed of an array of double square loops disposed over a dielectric substrate. In this study, the full ground plane is replaced with a periodic array to reflect only the frequencies of interest. By breaking the symmetry of the resonators and inserting PIN diodes for control, we demonstrate that the structure can efficiently absorb electromagnetic waves (PIN diode ON), convert the polarization (PIN diode OFF) and allow signals to travel in other frequency band. The simulated structure showed good results for both absorption and conversion. For the frequency of 3.05GHz the absorption rate was 97 %, and a conversion ratio of 98 % is obtained for the resonance frequency of 4.37GHz. Furthermore, the proposed structure has a thickness of lambda/30.7 in relation to the absorption peak. Although the operating bands are narrow, the structure has potential applications such as thermal detectors, stealth field, imaging, remote sensors, and radiometers.

articleTitle: Broadband Negative Capacitors Based on NIC with the Darlington Transistors
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: Broadband non-Foster negative capacitors for the megahertz and gigahertz ranges based on a negative impedance converter (NIC) with composite transistors are presented. A modified Darlington transistor which features a high-impedance RLC-circuit to supply additional current to emitters is employed. A significant extension of the operating bandwidth of the negative capacitors is demonstrated when using NIC with the modified Darlington transistors.

articleTitle: Numerical Investigation of Metal-Organic-Framework Coated Long-Period Fiber Grating for CO2 Gas Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: We propose a novel sensor design utilizing metal-organic-framework (MOF) coated long-period fiber grating (LPFG) for carbon dioxide (CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) gas detection. This sensor exploits the coupling between the fundamental core mode (LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf>) and the higher-order cladding mode (LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">07</inf>). Both modes exhibit distinct spectral variations in their propagation characteristics when CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>is adsorbed in the MOF layer due to their differing penetration depths within the MOF. Consequently, the phasematching point is shifted, yielding an 8 nm wavelength shift in the transmission dip.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Battery Consumption and Jitter Between ViNR and VoNR over IMS 5G Network
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: Video conferencing is widely used for quick communication, like in meetings held at a distance. Both the Quality of Service (QoS) and user expectations must be met by this feature. The major objective of this study is to evaluate the energy consumption and jitter of a real-time testbed for Video Over New Radio (ViNR) during an IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS) video session. The information shows that ViNR can drain the battery up to 161.08% faster than Voice Over New Radio (VoNR). This research demonstrates that the jitter values for voice and video are nearly equivalent, gives information on measuring jitter for video conversations, analyzes power usage for ViNR, and quantifies jitter values.

articleTitle: Diffraction Grating-Based Tool for Spectral Characterization of THz Beams
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: The spectroscopic tool for the analysis of narrow-band THz beams is proposed. It is based on a single diffraction grating and one moving element (rotary or transitional stage). Two configurations - transmissive and reflective - are analyzed and compared. Compared with commercially available spectro-scopes, the setup is simple, cost-effective, and easily adapted to the given conditions. The obtained experimental error of the frequency prediction was as low as 0.19%.

articleTitle: Analyzing Machine Learning Paradigms for the Linearization of 5G Radio over Fiber Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This work presents the use, analyses and proposals of improvement of Machine Learning (ML) techniques for compensating nonlinearities from the fifth generation of mobile communications (5G) Radio-over-Fiber (RoF) systems.
