RoF- based transmission networks enable us to take advantage of the high bandwidth of optical systems and the flexibility of wireless transmission. However, integrating these systems generates non-linear distortions in the modulated signal. We assess three machine-learning techniques to correct these nonlinearities, one based on Support Vector (SV), another based on regression trees, and a third based on Artificial Neural Networks (ANN). We apply them to an Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) and investigate its performance based on two metrics, the Mean Squared Error (MSE) and the Power Spectral Density (PSD). We demonstrate ANN provides enhanced performance for this task, by means of providing 53% improvement in the MSE parameter and maintaining the low-complexity approach.

articleTitle: Data Rates and UE Current Consumption Analysis in 5G NSA over Millimeter Waves
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This paper aims to analyze the performance of 5G New Radio (NR) user equipment (UE), under non-standalone (NSA) deployment, in terms of both the achievable data rates and current consumption in scenarios of Carrier aggregation (CA) over millimeter wave bands. The results generated through laboratory measurements and compared to simulations, show that 5G UE may achieve data rates of around 8 Gbps by aggregating 8 Component Carriers (CCs). Also, this analysis quantifies the UE current consumption in different scenarios of network configurations, e.g., number of multiple input-multiple output (MIMO) antennas, modulation schemes and number of aggregated CCs. In addition to showing a direct proportionality relation between the allocated resources and current consumption, the results show that Carrier aggregation may cause up to 70% higher current consumption than the modulation scheme and number of MIMO antennas.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Two Reflection Amplifier Topologies for Low Power Backscattering Tag Design
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This work studies enhancing bistatic backscatter communication systems by integrating a reflection amplifier in the hardware front-end of the transponder. Two reflection amplifier prototypes have been designed, manufactured, and characterized following the two primary topologies: tunnel diode-based reflection amplifiers and bipolar transistor-based reflection amplifiers. The advantages and disadvantages of both amplifiers have been discussed. Additionally, a phase-shift modulator has been designed to modulate the backscattering tag, generating two antipodal reflection coefficients in the Smith chart, thereby maximizing its differential radar cross-section.

articleTitle: A Novel Cantor-Inspired Fractal for Wideband Mutual Coupling Reduction Between Closely-Spaced Patches in MIMO Microstrip Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel structure for wideband mutual coupling reduction between multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) microstrip antenna arrays with elliptical patch elements. The proposed structure utilizes Cantor's fractal with dynamic parameters to effectively decouple an average of 25 dB of transmission between the antenna array elements. Simulations using Ansys HFSS software were conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed structure. Additionally, prototypes were fabricated and measured to validate the simulation results, demonstrating good agreement between the simulated and measured outcomes. Furthermore, the proposed antenna array design exhibits improvements in mutual coupling reduction, size reduction, and overall performance compared to traditional Cantor's fractal antenna array designs.

articleTitle: Development and Characterization of Wideband Power Divider for Sub-THz Transceiver Modules
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: In this work, the development and characterization of a wideband power divider for Sub-THz applications have been presented. The divider is aimed to be used for dividing the IF signal at 50 GHz with a bandwidth of 40 GHz. The design is implemented on a low transmission loss 8-layers PCB whose modeling methodology will be highlighted. The design conceptually is based on shifting down the isolation plane below 90 degree length while utilizing a radial stub for compensating the change in the isolation element. The preliminary analysis for the design had been studied for a single stage model while the optimized design is measured back-to-back configuration and showed a good agreement to the simulation. The proposed design is implemented in a 275 GHz receiver module of multiple CMOS mixer chips fed from phased array antenna for enabling beamforming capability.

articleTitle: Fiber-Optic and IMU Sensors for Muscle Fatigue Detection in Work Settings
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: Detection of muscle fatigue is essential in industrial environments to prevent work-related disorders and improve worker safety. Also, measuring elbow position is essential in human motion analysis. This paper proposes a novel approach for detecting muscle fatigue using an Optical Fiber (OF) sensor and Inertial Measurement Unit sensors (IMU). Ten healthy subjects performed a repetitive lifting activity using the IMU and OF sensor until reaching muscle fatigue. The study evaluates four machine learning algorithms, including Ensemble Classifiers (EC), Support Vector Machine (SVM), k Nearest Neighbour (kNN), and Neural Networks (NN). Results of detecting muscle fatigue using the OF and IMU sensors obtained an accuracy of 98.4%. This setup can be easily used by workers and be relevant to identify workers' fatigue during long working shifts.

articleTitle: Yagi-Uda Antenna Array Gain Optimization by the PSO and ES Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)

authors.preferredName: L. R. G. S. Lourenço Novo

abstract: Optimizing antenna arrays for beamforming and also beamsteering comprises to determine the optimal electromagnetic parameters for the antennas feeding. The primary goal is to focus the main lobe towards the desired directions while minimizing energy losses in the undesired ones. In this research, two evolutionary algorithms, namely Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Evolution Strategies (ES), were applied to optimize a four-element Yagi-Uda antenna array. The results demonstrate the robustness and feasibility of both algorithms for this application, whose the best algorithm depends on the requirements. While PSO exhibits superior accuracy, ES provides a faster estimation way.

articleTitle: Proposal of a Fiber/Wireless System Assisted by Machine Learning Towards 6G Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This paper reports the performance evaluation of a fiber/wireless (FiWi) system assisted by a machine learning (ML) algorithm envisioned for the sixth generation of mobile networks (6G). An augmented real-valued time delay neural network (ARVTDNN) is trained to learn the inverse response of the non-linear distortions introduced by the communication chain. The trained ML algorithm operates as a digital pre-distortion (DPD) scheme, which allows an analog radio-over-fiber (A-RoF) system to be used to connect the central office (CO) with a low-cost remote radio head (RRH) installed in remote areas. A Rayleigh channel was employed to model the wireless radio-frequency (RF) signal transmission. The RF signal is linearized by the DPD scheme before being radiated, aiming to provide broadband communications for remote and rural areas. Numerical results demonstrate that the ML-based DPD scheme enables the seamless integration of A-RoF into the wireless system.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable U-Shaped Microwave Resonator for the Construction of a Hydrogen Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This paper describes the design, parameter optimization and simulation of a resonant device using the CST Studio Suite for the development of a sensor capable of detecting hydrogen at microwave frequencies. The device is reconfigurable as it comprises a U-shaped resonator that can slide relative to a static stripline. As a result of this strategy, it is possible to investigate a configuration that yields the best response for hydrogen detection, taking into account the frequency variation and insertion loss induced by hydrogen gas on the palladium present in the device.

articleTitle: PoF System Using Standard 62.5-Micron Multimode Fiber for 5G NR Industrial Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This paper presents an experimental implementation of a radio-over-fiber (RoF)-based 5G new radio (NR) system and power-over-fiber (PoF) technique for industrial environ-ments. The generated 3.5-GHz 5G NR signal is transmitted throughout a 20-km single-mode optical fiber (SMF) link. Re-garding the PoF system, a 5-W optical power is transmitted by means of a 100-m standard multimode optical fiber (MMF) link. A photovoltaic power converter (PPC) and a DC/DC converter are employed to convert the power from the optical to the electrical domain and adjust the voltage level, respectively, aiming to power an RoF module. As a result, the PoF system power transmission efficiency (PTE) is analyzed, reaching a mean value of around 19%, and root mean square error vector magnitude (EVM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RMs</inf>) performance investigation is conducted to evaluate the 5G transmission. A throughput of 600 Mbps is achieved with 100-MHz bandwidth and without performance degradation when compared to the conventionally powered RoF system, demonstrating the applicability and potential of the PoF technique for 5G NR-based industrial communications.

articleTitle: Shape-Morphing Polymers for Tunable Frequency Selective Surfaces and Reflectarray Elements
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This work presents a route to rapidly configuring electromagnetic metamaterials and elements such as reflectarrays from a generic ‘blank’. The concept is based upon the thermal-shrinkage properties of prestrained polystyrene (PPS), which is utilized in two distinct designs: In the first, an array of resonant split rings is printed upon a sheet of PPS. It is shown that heating to near the glass transition temperature of the sheet can controllably shrink the entire structure, thereby tuning its spectral transmission or reflection. A second application is to make coupled resonant elements, one of which is placed on a hinge of PPS that can be deformed via optical illumination, providing an optical route to tuning the resonance. This kind of element can show a large range of phase shifts in the reflected radiation, and opens the door to the creation of optically configurable reflectarrays.

articleTitle: Acoustic Data Communication Over a Stainless Metallic Rod
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This article describes the use of a stainless steel rod as a communication medium for a low-rate system. The setup has been evaluated as a proof of concept using a two transducers configuration. Acoustic data is transmitted axially, along the longer dimension of the rod. Experimental setup reaches up to 400 kbit/s for a BER of 1 error out of 1 million bits.

articleTitle: Optimized Two-Stage Few-Mode Erbium Doped Fiber Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: Few-mode erbium-doped fiber amplifiers (FM-EDFAs) are key elements in the development of Space Division Multiplexing systems based on few-mode fibers. In this work, through numerical simulation, we designed a two-stage FM-EDFA, minimizing both the differential spectral gain (DSG) and the differential modal gain (DMG) by means of a gain-flattening filter and pumping optimized through a genetic algorithm. By propagating 9 WDM signals in each of 6 LP modes and using 3 pumping modes, we kept the DMG and DSG below 3 dB and 0.6 dB, respectively; with a mean gain 17 dB and NF below 5 dB, along the all C- band.

articleTitle: A Power Efficient Quadruple Time- Interleaved 2.5 GS/s 7 bit SAR ADC with Real-Time Data Output
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This paper presents the design and measurement results of a 2.5 GS/s 7 bit successive approximation register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC) with real-time data output using the JESD204B protocol. It is implemented as quadruple time interleaved ADC in a 22 nm fully-depleted silicon-on-insulator technology and consumes 43mW overall, while the analog frontend (ADC cores and interleaver) consumes only 7.8mW. Up to the Nyquist frequency, the effective number of bits is larger than 6.1 bit leading to a Walden Figure-of-Merit of 45 fJ/conv.-step and a Schreier Figure-of-Merit of 150.5 dB. Integral and differential nonlinearity are both well below 0.5 LSB for all measurement scenarios.

articleTitle: Development of a Textile Device Applied to Hand Gesture Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel chip-free textile tag for gesture recognition applications. The proposed tag consists of a frequency selective surface (FSS) printed on the fabric with conductive ink. The transmission coefficients of the device proposed are controlled by each finger position. This is achieved by associating each finger phalanx with a conductive element. The authors present and discuss a two-finger prototype that was fabricated from fabric commonly used in the textile industry, the jeans. The results obtained demonstrate that the proposed device has a high degree of applicability in gesture recognition applications.

articleTitle: Analysis of a Microwave Filter Parameters for Design Optimization via Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)

authors.preferredName: J. M. A. M. De Oliveira

abstract: Microwave filters are essential for filtering and selecting frequencies. They prevent interference, enhance signal quality, and maximize the efficiency of microwave systems. They are widely employed in wireless communications, satellites, and radar systems. To optimize the design of these filters, techniques like machine learning can be utilized, saving time and resources compared to simulations. Machine learning learns from data to discover optimized solutions more swiftly and efficiently, leading to high-performance filters. In this work, analyses of the parameters of a T-inverted filter were performed to serve as a foundation for a machine learning-based design. The filter used was designed and manufactured for a frequency range of 1 GHz to 3 GHz and its measured and simulated results were compared as a way of validating the structure.

articleTitle: Integrated Dual-Band Monopole Antenna with Frequency Selective Surface for Non-Invasive Biomedical Sensor Application
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)

authors.preferredName: Antônio Luiz Pereira De Siqueira Campos

abstract: This work proposes the integration of a monopole antenna with a frequency selective surface (FSS) with double square loop geometry, which operates in the ISM (2.4 – 2.4835 GHz) and IEEE 802.11 WLAN (5.15-5.725 GHz) bands. The FSS was developed to be integrated into a microstrip monopole antenna, aiming to improve some of its radiative features, such as gain, directivity and front-to-back ratio (RFC). We show that the double square loop FSS operates in the bands from 1.91 to 3 GHz and from 4.64 to 6.56 GHz, fully covering the bands of interest. A prototype of the proposed structure was assembled and both the numerical simulation and the experimental results show that the antenna integrated with FSS presents significant improvements in all parameters, compared to the antenna without FSS.

articleTitle: Wireless Channel Characterization Using a Vector Network Analyzer
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: Wireless channel characterization is a relevant task in order to optimize its maximum data transfer. Two different basic techniques are used for it, based in the time and frequency domains. This article covers the latter case, finding the expressions relating the scattering parameter measurement and channel impulse response. A numerical simulation is presented to back the found expressions and a real-world indoor measurement is also presented, using a portable network analyzer.

articleTitle: Frequency Tunable QMSIW-Based Antenna Using Liquid Dielectric for S-Band applications
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This paper presents a simple frequency tunable antenna using distilled water. The antenna model is based on Quarter-mode substrate integrated waveguide (QM-SIW) cavity. The antenna is simulated using electromagnetic simulation software (HFSS) by exciting the cavity using the microstrip feed line. Three rectangular fluidic channels are incorporated into the dielectric substrate to provide frequency tunability. The resonant frequency can be tuned by filling distilled water in each channel. The proposed antenna exhibits tuning from 2.5 to 3.5 GHz with gain varying in the range of 3.87 - 5.85 dBi. A prototype has been fabricated using a Rogers 5880 substrate, and the results from simulations and actual measurements show close correlation. This antenna model has a simple, compact design with frequency flexibility that can be used in various S-band applications.

articleTitle: Disjoint-Path Groups Routing for Multipath Protection in Elastic Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel routing algorithm which enables the fixed-alternate routing by using ordered groups of link-disjoint paths in order to improve the RSA process in multipath protection approach.

articleTitle: Stress Classification Using a Low-Cost Optical Fiber Physiological Sensor: A Preliminary Study
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: The classification and measurement of stress through physiological sensors have been studied because of their high impact on mental health and well-being. Low-cost optical fiber wearable sensors, can monitor signals and be adaptive systems. Therefore, the present study sought to evaluate a lowcost optical fiber physiological sensor developed for stress classification while monitoring physiological signals. Five volunteers participated in a stress-induced test, where pulse and respiratory measurements were correctly performed with the optical fiber sensor during both stress and relaxation. The data obtained were used to find the best machine-learning classification algorithm for stress detection: a Bagged Decision Tree Classifier with an accuracy of 88%, and a precision of 91%. Thus, the proposed sensor can effectively monitor pulse and respiratory signals for stress classification. Based on these results, a study with more volunteers will be performed.

articleTitle: Monoflow Measurement with Polarization Controlled Effect in SMS and SMSMS Optical Fiber Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This paper describes an experimental analysis of optical fiber sensors based on multimodal interference phenomenon using the core diameter mismatch technique, acting as a Mach-Zehnder interferometer. The sensor is composed of single-mode and multimode fibers that are spliced together and is used to measure monoflow fluids in pipeline systems. The research presents a comparison of two different sensors, one singlemode-multimode-singlemode (SMS) fibers structure and another singlemode-multimode-singlemode-multimode-singlemode (SMSMS) fibers structure applied to measure water flow, and there is also the control of the polarization effect in the sensing environment. The obtained results showed that the sensitivities values are affected by the influence of the polarizer device along the sensors path, with significant increase in the sensitivity from -2.206 dB.h/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> to 0.782 dB. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h$</tex>/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> with acceptable good linearity of 0.98 and 0.97 for the SMS sensor; for the SMSMS sensor, the sensitivity values changed from 0.862 dB.h/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> to 1.122 dB. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h$</tex>/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, with R2 = 0.99. The behavior and results proved that the use of a polarizer device keeps the polarization mode by inducing a uniform birefringence along the entire fiber and sensor which maintains and controls the optical power, thereby preventing random power coupling between polarization modes.

articleTitle: Analysis of LoRa Energy Autonomy Extension Using a Photovoltaic Power Supply System
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This work describes a methodology for characterizing the consumption of a Low Power Wide Area (LPWA) device based on LoRa (Long Range) technology and the possibility of integrating a Photovoltaic (PV) power supply system to extend its autonomy. The device consumption profiles for Transmission (TX) and Reception (RX) modes were measured, the I-V curves of the PV module were extracted to determine the Maximum Power Point (MPP), and the device autonomy was estimated for different scenarios. The results demonstrated that the autonomy of the LPWA device, both in TX and RX modes, can be extended using the PV power supply system under study through different battery and PV module use strategies.

articleTitle: Two-Section Branch-Line Coupler with Optimal Performance for Dual-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a two-section 90° hybrid coupler in microstrip technology for dual-band applications. In contrast to the standard design found in the literature, whereby the performance is optimized at a central frequency, the proposed approach aims at performance optimization in two different bands. The application aimed in this work is to feed navigation antennas, which should operate in two bands centered at 1.176 GHz (L5 band) and 1.575 GHz (L1 band). The design is done using the electromagnetic simulator ANSYS HFSS. Validation of the proposed design has been achieved by fabrication of a prototype and good agreement between simulated and measured results has been achieved. The measured output power unbalances are 0.67 dB in the L1 band and 0.18 dB in the L5 band. The reflection coefficient was below −20 dB in both bands, hence indicating that the design strategy was successful.

articleTitle: Condition Assessment of AC Contactors Using Optical Fiber Sensors and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: Electromechanical contactors are core equipment of the electrical circuits environment, operating mainly in industrial areas for load control. As they have a lifespan and are susceptible to faults, predictive maintenance based on measurement systems is crucial to avoid accidents and profit loss. This paper presents a method of instrumentation and analysis of AC contactors under different operational conditions. Optical Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) sensors were used as sensor elements. The experimental setup relied on two ABB AX40 AC contactors, each instrumented using a single FBG sensor externally. The devices were subjected to three switching conditions: the contactor with no faults, worn load contact, and end-life load contact. The events were submitted to different variability conditions to better generalize the system for field application. Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT) generated scalograms from the acquired signals to be submitted to different Convolution Neural Networks (CNNs) models. The data set was split between the training, CNN validation, and repeatability test groups. This third group is a set of conditions not trained with the classifier to verify the generalization. The results presented in this paper show a high F1 score of around 0.9 for the CNN architectures in the training group and validation groups. However the repeatability test group had lower results, being around 0.3. This paper shows the high applicability of FBG as single sensor element and CNN to monitoring and classifying faults in electrical switching devices, with further studies aiming for field application.

articleTitle: Flatness Analysis of Optical Frequency Combs Generated by Electro-Optical Modulators Using Unsupervised Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference (IMOC)
abstract: An approach is proposed to generate flat optical frequency combs (OFCs) by analyzing data from electro-optic modulator (EOM) modeling via unsupervised learning (UL) techniques. The comb spectral line (SL) amplitude information of OFCs produced by either a phase modulator (PM) or a dual-drive Mach-Zehnder modulator (DD-MZM) was obtained from the response analysis of both modulators. Then, the resulting data were evaluated by UL tools, enabling the generation of flat OFCs by each EOM. Separate experimental tests were conducted with a PM and an DD-MZM, resulting in the generation of optical combs with equalization of their most central lines. A positive correlation with the proposed approach is demonstrated by these results.
